sentences.text: Archaeorhynchus is a genus of beaked avialans that lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
Fossils of this creature preserve feathers on the neck, head, and tail regions.
Grooves and foramina on the jaw tips suggest the animal supported a horny bill.
Archaeorhynchus was a medium-sized avialan measuring approximately 20 cm in length, 15.5 cm in hip height, and weighing 275 grams.
The finger bones of Archaeorhynchus show a phalangeal formula of 2-3-2.
A 2021 study suggests Archaeorhynchus probably demonstrated flight soon after birth.
The genus Archaeorhynchus was first reported in 2005 by researchers Zhou and Zhang.
The type specimen of Archaeorhynchus spathula was found in the Yixian Formation at Yixian, Liaoning province, China.
Scientists hypothesize that Archaeorhynchus had an herbivorous diet based on the presence of numerous gastroliths in all known specimens.
Phylogenetic analysis indicates that Archaeorhynchus is most closely related to ornithurines.
Archaeorhynchus is classified within the unranked order Euornithes.
Archaeorhynchus lived from the Barremian to the Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 113.2 million years ago.
It is debated whether the gastroliths were swallowed accidentally or intentionally, though high numbers suggest the latter.
